identity.description: Setuid Rootshell Staged, Seen on the Linux Syslog Feed. The attacker behavior is visible in the Linux host auth/syslog that is forwarded to a Cortex Broker VM syslog applet (parsed into dataset=linux_syslog) — a collector/log-level detection, not the endpoint-agent process feed. CortexSim drives linux_syslog_emitter.py to reproduce the detectable syslog telemetry; no real host is touched.

techniques.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Setuid and Setgid

payload.code:
# Collector/log-level validation — stream shape-true Linux auth/syslog to the lab Broker VM.
COLLECTOR="${BROKER_VM:-192.0.2.9}"
python3 core/eal_simulator/linux_syslog_emitter.py --collector "$COLLECTOR" --phase baseline --baseline-count 40
python3 core/eal_simulator/linux_syslog_emitter.py --collector "$COLLECTOR" --phase attack --which setuid-privesc

expected_artifacts.description: Linux syslog records for: Setuid Rootshell Staged, Seen on the Linux Syslog Feed.

manual_steps: Not authored. Write and test cleanup before promotion.

xql_queries.name: Setuid Permission Change on a File in a Writable Path
xql_queries.query:
dataset = linux_syslog
| filter message contains "setuid" and (message contains "/tmp/" or message contains "uid=0")
| comp count() as c by host, message
| filter c >= 1
